items.problem: CoreInputView.GetForCurrentView().TryShow(CoreInputViewKind.Emoji) was ported verbatim into Scenario4 and wrapped in an empty try/catch; it emits WUI0004 and no-ops at runtime.
items.evidence: build-output.txt: 'Scenario4_ShowView.xaml.cs(29,19): warning WUI0004: CoreInputView.GetForCurrentView() is UWP-only'; Scenario4_ShowView.xaml.cs line 29 uses try{ CoreInputView.GetForCurrentView().TryShow(...) }catch{}.
items.skill_search: grepped winui-uwp-migration for 'CoreInputView' and 'InputView' — zero hits in SKILL.md, MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md, scripts.
items.root_cause: CoreInputView is a view-bound UWP input surface with no *Interop.GetForWindow and no reachable Windows.UI.UIContext in WinUI 3 (UIElement.UIContext is absent), so GetForUIContext is unusable — there is no supported desktop path, and the skill says nothing, leaving the agent to guess (catch-and-ignore).
items.proposed_fix: Add a CoreInputView row to the GetForCurrentView Replacements table in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md stating there is no supported WinUI 3 desktop path (no GetForWindow interop; GetForUIContext needs a UIContext WinUI elements no longer expose) and that the correct action is to drop the dead call, not swallow it.
items.generalizes: Soft/touch-keyboard and emoji/handwriting input samples across the Windows-universal-samples set use CoreInputView; any migration hitting a view-bound API with no desktop equivalent needs an explicit 'no supported path — remove, don't swallow' verdict instead of silent no-ops.
